featured_reviews.name: Durga
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review as an admitted patient who expected transparency, communication, and basic patient care, but unfortunately my experience raised several concerns.

One of my concerns involved the handling of medical supplies during my admission. I noticed items being taken away from my room and, when questioned, I was informed that these were being collected as replacements for items provided by the hospital. However, this process was never explained to me in advance. As a patient, I believe there should be complete transparency regarding any consumables, IV fluids, or medical supplies being used and accounted for, especially when these may ultimately be reflected in the final bill. I had to proactively raise this concern with the hospital administration myself.

My primary concern, however, was regarding the gastroenterology consultation. Throughout the day, I was repeatedly informed by the nursing staff that the gastroenterologist would be visiting me. Whenever I followed up, I was told that the doctor would come but that no one knew when. Even at around 9:30 PM, I was still waiting for clarity regarding the visit.

When I approached the reception desk for an update, I was informed that the gastroenterologist does not usually visit on Saturdays. This directly contradicted the information I had been receiving throughout the day. When I questioned why conflicting information had been provided, the RMO, Dr. Drishti, intervened in the conversation.

Unfortunately, my interaction with Dr. Drishti was disappointing. I found her communication to be dismissive and lacking empathy towards an admitted patient who was unwell and seeking clarity regarding their treatment. Rather than addressing my concern regarding the contradictory information provided by the staff, I was simply told that the doctor would come and that his timing was not fixed. No clear explanation was provided regarding the consultation process, expected timeline, or next steps. Additionally, at no point did the RMO assess my condition, enquire about my health status, or provide reassurance despite my repeated concerns.

As a patient admitted under medical care, I expected better communication, coordination, and accountability. Patients should not be left waiting for hours without updates, nor should they receive conflicting information from different departments regarding specialist consultations.

I would like to acknowledge that several nurses and staff members were caring and professional, and the facilities themselves were good. However, transparency, communication, accountability, and patient engagement require significant improvement. Patients who are admitted, unwell, and paying for specialist care deserve timely information, clear communication, and respectful treatment.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Karuna Hospital in Borivali West is a well-known multi-speciality hospital that offers a wide range of medical services at relatively affordable costs. It has been serving patients for many years and is known for its compassionate approach towards treatment.

The hospital is equipped with essential facilities like ICU, operation theatres, CT scan, pathology lab, and in-house pharmacy, making it convenient for patients to get complete treatment under one roof.

Doctors are generally experienced and supportive, especially for general treatments and routine procedures. The hospital is also considered a good option for budget-friendly healthcare compared to premium hospitals in Mumbai.

However, during peak hours, waiting time can be long, and management/administration could be better organized. Cleanliness and infrastructure are decent but not at par with newer or high-end hospitals.

Overall, it’s a reliable option for affordable treatment and basic to moderate medical needs, but may not be the best choice if you’re looking for premium facilities or faster service.

Staying hydrated is just as important during the monsoon as it is in summer. Although the weather feels cooler, your body continues to lose fluids through daily activities. Proper hydration helps support normal body functions and overall well-being.

Here are a few simple tips to stay hydrated during the rainy season:

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.
🥥 Include fluids like coconut water, soups, or fresh fruit with high water content in your diet.
🍉 Eat seasonal fruits and vegetables after washing them thoroughly.
☕ Limit excessive caffeinated or sugary beverages, which may contribute to dehydration.
🧼 Carry a clean water bottle and maintain good hygiene to reduce the risk of waterborne illnesses.

Pay attention to signs such as excessive thirst, dark-colored urine, dizziness, or unusual fatigue, as these may indicate dehydration.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.
